sealedSource: Structurally modelled on launch decisions made under cold-weather component uncertainty where engineering objections were reversed under schedule pressure.
archetype: Reversed burden of proof; dialogue restriction; irreversible physical outcome.
historicallySupportedMechanisms: The burden of proof was reversed: uncertainty was treated as permission to proceed unless engineers could prove danger.
A supplier-management reversal was treated as if it resolved the underlying engineering evidence.
The launch environment lay outside the evidence envelope for reliable seal behaviour.
materialisedConsequences: Total loss of vehicle and payload
Programme suspension far exceeding the delay being avoided
irreversibleThreshold: Physical destruction of the vehicle — no recovery path of any kind.
absentStakeholder: The supplier's engineers, whose recommendation was overturned by their own management under customer pressure.
narratorContribution: The narrator inverted the burden of proof, requiring proof of danger rather than proof of safety, and treated a management reversal as engineering evidence.
horizonMismatch: Decision horizon 14 hours; recovery horizon for the programme was years; the narrator did not state one.

availableActionsAtDecisionPoint.action: Delay launch until temperatures rise, as the supplier engineers recommended.
Do not treat the supplier-management reversal as resolution of the engineering concern; require the cold-condition uncertainty to be resolved before launch.

plausibleUnrealisedRisks: Further delay could damage short-term commercial credibility and attract media criticism.
irrelevantDistractors: Payload-customer litigation as the principal mechanism
nonTargetHistoricalEvents: A supplier contract dispute occurred but was immaterial to the central harm.
